question:
All dogs are animals. All animals are living beings. Which conclusion follows?
A) All living beings are dogs
B) All dogs are living beings
C) Some living beings are not animals
D) No dogs are living beings

options.C: Some living beings are not animals

explanation: From 'All dogs are animals' and 'All animals are living beings', by universal syllogism, All dogs are living beings follows directly.

question:
No birds are fish. All fish are aquatic. Which conclusion must be true?
A) All aquatic creatures are fish
B) No birds are aquatic
C) Some aquatic creatures are not birds
D) All birds are aquatic

options.C: Some aquatic creatures are not birds

explanation: Since all fish are aquatic and no birds are fish, birds are excluded from the fish subset of aquatic creatures. So some aquatic creatures (namely fish) are not birds.

question:
Some teachers are singers. All singers are musicians. Some musicians are dancers. Which conclusion definitely follows?
A) Some teachers are musicians
B) All teachers are dancers
C) Some singers are dancers
D) All musicians are teachers
explanation: Since some teachers are singers and all singers are musicians, those teachers who are singers are also musicians. Hence, some teachers are musicians is a valid conclusion.

question:
All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. No red things are plastic. Which conclusion is definitely true?
A) All roses are red
B) Some roses are not plastic
C) No flowers are plastic
D) Some flowers are not red
explanation: Only 'some flowers are red' is given, which means some flowers are not red. This follows directly from the particular affirmative statement.

question:
If it rains, Zara carries an umbrella. Zara is not carrying an umbrella. What can we conclude?
A) It is raining
B) It is not raining
C) Zara forgot her umbrella
D) Nothing can be concluded
explanation: By modus tollens: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. Since Zara is not carrying an umbrella (not Q), it is not raining (not P).

question:
If a student passes the exam, they receive a certificate. Ali received a certificate. What can we conclude?
A) Ali passed the exam
B) Ali did not pass the exam
C) Ali may or may not have passed the exam
D) All students receive certificates

options.B: Ali did not pass the exam
options.C: Ali may or may not have passed the exam

explanation: Affirming the consequent is a fallacy. The certificate might have been given for another reason. We cannot confirm Ali passed just because he has a certificate.

question:
If P then Q. If Q then R. If R then S. P is true. Which of the following must be true?
A) P and S only
B) Q and R only
C) P, Q, R, and S
D) S only
explanation: By hypothetical syllogism: P is true → Q is true → R is true → S is true. All four statements must be true.

question:
Either the project is delayed or the team works overtime. The project is not delayed. What follows?
A) The team does not work overtime
B) The team works overtime
C) The project may still be delayed
D) Nothing can be determined

options.A: The team does not work overtime
options.C: The project may still be delayed

explanation: This is a disjunctive syllogism: P or Q; not P; therefore Q. Since the project is not delayed, the team must work overtime.

question:
Argument: Schools that adopt tablet-based learning see improved student performance. Therefore, all schools should adopt tablets.
Which statement most weakens this argument?
A) Tablets are expensive and many schools cannot afford them
B) Some students prefer physical textbooks
C) The improved performance was only observed in well-funded private schools
D) Tablets can be used for non-educational purposes

options.A: Tablets are expensive and many schools cannot afford them
options.C: The improved performance was only observed in well-funded private schools
options.D: Tablets can be used for non-educational purposes

explanation: If the performance improvement only occurred in well-resourced private schools, the conclusion that all schools should adopt tablets does not follow, as the results may not generalize.

question:
Claim: Regular exercise reduces the risk of heart disease.
Which finding most strengthens this claim?
A) Many athletes have healthy hearts
B) A 20-year longitudinal study found sedentary individuals had 3x higher rates of heart disease than those exercising regularly
C) Doctors recommend exercise
D) Heart disease rates vary by country

options.B: A 20-year longitudinal study found sedentary individuals had 3x higher rates of heart disease than those exercising regularly
options.D: Heart disease rates vary by country

explanation: A controlled longitudinal study directly comparing sedentary and active populations provides strong causal evidence supporting the claim.

question:
Argument: City X banned plastic bags and subsequently littering decreased by 40%. Therefore, banning plastic bags reduces littering.
Which of the following most seriously weakens this conclusion?
A) Other cities have also banned plastic bags
B) At the same time as the ban, City X launched a major anti-littering campaign and doubled fines
C) Some residents opposed the ban
D) Plastic bags are still sold in neighbouring cities

options.A: Other cities have also banned plastic bags
options.B: At the same time as the ban, City X launched a major anti-littering campaign and doubled fines
options.D: Plastic bags are still sold in neighbouring cities

explanation: The simultaneous anti-littering campaign and increased fines are confounding variables. The decrease in littering could be due to these factors rather than the plastic bag ban itself.

question:
The new medicine has been proven effective in laboratory tests. Therefore, it will be effective for human patients.
What assumption does this argument make?
A) Laboratory tests are always reliable
B) Results from laboratory tests translate to human patients
C) The medicine has no side effects
D) Human patients have agreed to take the medicine

options.B: Results from laboratory tests translate to human patients
options.C: The medicine has no side effects
options.D: Human patients have agreed to take the medicine

explanation: The argument jumps from lab results to human effectiveness, assuming the two are comparable. This bridging assumption is necessary for the conclusion to hold.

question:
Since the unemployment rate fell last quarter, the government's economic policy is working.
Which assumption underlies this argument?
A) The government caused the drop in unemployment
B) Unemployment is the only measure of economic health
C) The policy was implemented last quarter
D) The unemployment rate will continue to fall

options.A: The government caused the drop in unemployment
options.B: Unemployment is the only measure of economic health
options.C: The policy was implemented last quarter
options.D: The unemployment rate will continue to fall

explanation: The argument attributes falling unemployment to government policy, assuming the government's actions caused the change rather than other economic factors.

question:
Ahmed scored higher than Bilal on the entrance test, so Ahmed is more qualified for the position.
Which assumption is necessary for this conclusion?
A) The entrance test accurately measures qualifications for the position
B) Bilal did not study for the test
C) Ahmed and Bilal applied for the same position
D) The position only requires academic ability

options.A: The entrance test accurately measures qualifications for the position
options.B: Bilal did not study for the test
options.C: Ahmed and Bilal applied for the same position
options.D: The position only requires academic ability

explanation: For the test score to determine qualifications, we must assume the test is a valid measure of the relevant qualifications. Without this assumption, the conclusion does not follow.

question:
Paradox: Country A spends twice as much per student on education as Country B, yet Country B consistently outperforms Country A in international math rankings.
Which explains this paradox?
A) Country A has more students
B) Country B has more experienced teachers and a culture that values academic achievement
C) Country A spends money on sports
D) International rankings are unreliable

options.B: Country B has more experienced teachers and a culture that values academic achievement
options.C: Country A spends money on sports

explanation: Spending alone does not guarantee outcomes. Country B's advantage in teacher quality and cultural emphasis on education explains better performance despite lower spending.

question:
Paradox: A hospital introduced a new protocol to reduce infection rates. After one month, infection rates at the hospital increased.
Which of the following best explains this paradox?
A) The hospital is old
B) The protocol was not followed correctly
C) The hospital began accepting more patients with existing infections from other facilities
D) Doctors were on vacation

options.B: The protocol was not followed correctly
options.C: The hospital began accepting more patients with existing infections from other facilities

explanation: If the hospital started admitting more patients who already had infections, the overall infection rate would rise even if the protocol worked for internally acquired infections.

question:
A company improved working conditions and increased salaries, yet employee productivity fell in the following quarter.
Which best resolves this paradox?
A) The company hired too many new employees
B) Employees became complacent due to job security and reduced effort since they were no longer motivated by fear of losing their jobs
C) The office relocated to a new building
D) The market demand decreased

options.A: The company hired too many new employees
options.B: Employees became complacent due to job security and reduced effort since they were no longer motivated by fear of losing their jobs
options.C: The office relocated to a new building

explanation: This explains the paradox using the concept of reduced extrinsic motivation. When job security improved, fear-based motivation decreased, causing a temporary productivity drop.

question:
A table shows monthly sales:
Jan: 200, Feb: 250, Mar: 300, Apr: 350, May: 400
What is the average monthly sales for Jan–May?
A) 280
B) 300
C) 320
D) 350

A pie chart shows departmental budget allocation: HR 15%, IT 25%, Operations 35%, Marketing 20%, R&D 5%. If the total budget is Rs. 80,00,000, how much is allocated to IT and Marketing combined?
A) Rs. 28,00,000
B) Rs. 36,00,000
C) Rs. 40,00,000
D) Rs. 32,00,000

The following data shows the number of books read by 5 students: Ayesha: 12, Bilal: 8, Camil: 15, Danish: 10, Erum: 5. What percentage of the total books read were read by Camil?
A) 25%
B) 30%
C) 20%
D) 15%
explanation: Total = 12+8+15+10+5 = 50. Camil read 15. Percentage = 15/50 × 100 = 30%.

question:
A bar chart shows exports (in million USD): 2019: 120, 2020: 90, 2021: 130, 2022: 160, 2023: 150. What is the percentage increase in exports from 2020 to 2022?
A) 66.7%
B) 77.8%
C) 55.6%
D) 70%

Five friends — A, B, C, D, E — sit in a row. A sits at one end. B sits next to A. C sits at the other end. D and E sit between B and C. Who sits in the middle?
A) D
B) E
C) B
D) Cannot be determined
explanation: The arrangement is A-B-?-?-C. D and E fill positions 3 and 4, but their relative order is not specified. The middle seat (position 3) could be either D or E.

question:
Six people P, Q, R, S, T, U sit in a row facing north. P is 3rd from the left. Q is to the immediate right of P. R sits at the rightmost end. S is 2nd from the left. T and U fill the remaining seats. How many people sit between S and R?
A) 2
B) 3
C) 4
D) 1
explanation: Positions: 1-? 2-S 3-P 4-Q 5-? 6-R. S is at 2, R is at 6. Between positions 2 and 6, there are positions 3,4,5 = 3 people... wait: P(3), Q(4), and one of T/U(5) = 3 people between S and R. Answer is B(3). Let me recount: 2 to 6 exclusive = positions 3,4,5 = 3 people. Answer: B.

question:
Seven boxes are stacked vertically labeled 1 (top) to 7 (bottom). Box A is immediately above Box C. Box B is 3rd from the top. Box C is 5th from the top. Which box is immediately below Box B?
A) Box D
B) Cannot be determined
C) Box A
D) Box C
explanation: Box C is 5th from top. Box A is immediately above C, so A is at position 4. Box B is at position 3. Position 4 is immediately below position 3. Therefore Box A is immediately below Box B.

question:
Four people A, B, C, D sit around a circular table. A sits opposite C. B sits to the immediate left of A. Who sits to the immediate right of A?
A) B
B) C
C) D
D) Cannot be determined
explanation: A sits opposite C. B is to A's immediate left. With 4 seats, D must be to A's immediate right (the only remaining person).

question:
Six people P, Q, R, S, T, U sit around a circular table facing the centre. P sits opposite T. Q sits to the immediate left of P. R sits opposite Q. S and U fill the remaining seats. S sits to the immediate right of T. Who sits opposite S?
A) P
B) Q
C) U
D) R
explanation: With 6 people, arrange: P opposite T, Q left of P, R opposite Q. Remaining: S and U. S is right of T. In a 6-seat circle, opposite S would be U (the remaining person placed 3 seats from S).

question:
Eight people A–H sit in a circle facing outward (backs to centre). A is between B and C. D is 3 seats clockwise from A. E sits opposite A. F is between D and G. H and G are adjacent. How many people sit between B and E going clockwise from B?
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 4
explanation: With 8 seats, E is opposite A (4 seats away). B is adjacent to A. Going clockwise from B to E, we pass through 3 intermediate people (in the half circle not containing C and A).

question:
Pointing to a man in a photo, Sara said 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is Sara related to the man?
A) Aunt
B) Sister
C) Mother
D) Grandmother
explanation: The only daughter of Sara's mother is Sara herself. So the man's mother is Sara. Therefore Sara is the man's mother.

question:
A + B means A is the father of B. A - B means A is the sister of B. If P + Q - R, what is P to R?
A) Uncle
B) Father
C) Grandfather
D) Brother
explanation: P + Q means P is the father of Q. Q - R means Q is the sister of R. So P is the father of Q, who is the sister of R. Therefore P is the father of R's sister, making P the uncle (or father) of R. Since Q is a sister (female), P is the uncle of R... actually P is R's father since P is Q's father and Q is R's sister. Wait — P + Q means P is father of Q; Q - R means Q is sister of R, so Q and R share the same parents, meaning P is R's father too. Answer: B.

question:
Introducing Hamza, Fatima says, 'He is the son of the only son of my grandfather.' How is Hamza related to Fatima?
A) Brother
B) Uncle
C) Cousin
D) Father
explanation: Fatima's grandfather's only son is Fatima's father. Hamza is the son of Fatima's father. So Hamza is Fatima's brother.

question:
In a family, there are 6 members: A, B, C, D, E, F. A and B are a married couple. C is the son of B. D is the brother of A. E is the daughter of C. F is the wife of D. How is E related to D?
A) Niece
B) Daughter
C) Grand-niece
D) Cousin
explanation: E is C's daughter. C is B's son. B is married to A. D is A's brother. So D is uncle of C (A's brother = C's uncle). E is C's daughter, making E the grand-niece of D.

question:
Raza starts walking North. He turns right, then turns right again, then turns left. In which direction is he now walking?
A) North
B) South
C) East
D) West
explanation: Start: North. Right turn → East. Right turn → South. Left turn → East. Final direction: East.

question:
Amna walks 5 km East, then 3 km North, then 5 km West. How far is she from the starting point?
A) 3 km
B) 5 km
C) 8 km
D) 13 km
explanation: East 5 km, then West 5 km cancels out. She ends up 3 km North of the starting point. Distance = 3 km.

question:
Khalid walks 10 km South, then turns left and walks 6 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. How far is he from the starting point, and in which direction?
A) 6 km West
B) 6 km East
C) 6 km North
D) 4 km East
explanation: Start → 10 km South → turns left (East) → 6 km East → turns left (North) → 10 km North. Net vertical: 10S + 10N = 0. Net horizontal: 6 East. Final position: 6 km East of start.

question:
In the morning, Tariq stands facing his shadow. In which direction is he facing?
A) North
B) South
C) East
D) West
explanation: In the morning, the sun rises in the East. Shadows fall to the West. If Tariq faces his shadow, he is facing West.

question:
In a certain code, MANGO is written as NAMHP. How is APPLE written in that code?
A) BQPMF
B) BQQMF
C) AQQLF
D) BPPLE
explanation: Each letter is shifted by +1 for odd positions and -1 for even positions: M+1=N, A-1=@(skip), wait — check: M→N(+1), A→A(0)?, N→H(-6)? Let me re-examine: MANGO→NAMHP: M→N(+1), A→A(0)... Actually: M(13)→N(14)+1, A(1)→N(14)+13? No. Looking at each: M→N(+1), A→M-1? Let's use shift: each letter +1: M→N, A→B, N→O, G→H, O→P = NBOHP. Not matching. Try: swap adjacent pairs: MA→AM, NG→GN, O→P? M↔A = AM, N↔G = GN, O→P... AMGNP? No. MANGO → NAMHP: N=M+1, A=A, M=N-1, H=G+1, P=O+1. Pattern: +1,-1 alternating skipping middle? Actually: position 1: +1, position 2: no change→A stays A, position 3: -1 (N→M), position 4: +1 (G→H), position 5: +1 (O→P). APPLE: A+1=B, P+0=P, P-1=O, L+1=M, E+1=F = BPOMF. Closest is A: BQPMF. The exact pattern may encode +1 always: A→B, P→Q, P→Q, L→M, E→F = BQQMF. Answer B.

question:
If CAT = 3120, DOG = 4157, then FAN = ?
A) 6114
B) 6120
C) 5114
D) 6214
explanation: Each letter is coded as its alphabetic position: C=3, A=1, T=20 → 3120. D=4, O=15, G=7 → 4157. F=6, A=1, N=14 → 6114.

question:
In a code language, '123' means 'bright winter day', '345' means 'day is cold', '246' means 'bright sunny morning'. What is the code for 'winter'?
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 4
explanation: '123' = bright winter day. 'day' appears in '123' and '345', so 'day' = 3. 'bright' appears in '123' and '246', so 'bright' = 2. Therefore 'winter' = 1.

question:
If STRONG is coded as ROTNSG, what is the code for WINTER?
A) IWTNRE
B) IWNTRE
C) ENWIRT
D) IWNTSR
explanation: STRONG → ROTNSG: S↔R swap positions 1&2, T stays, O↔N swap positions 4&5, S→S, G stays... Actually: S(1)R(2)O(3)N(4)G(5) rearranged as R(2)O(3)T... Let me check: STRONG=S,T,R,O,N,G → ROTNSG=R,O,T,N,S,G. Mapping: position 1→R(was pos3), 2→O(was pos4)... Rearrangement is 3,4,2,5,1,6. WINTER=W,I,N,T,E,R → apply 3,4,2,5,1,6: N,T,I,E,W,R = NTIEWR. Not in options. Try pairs swap: ST→TS, RO→OR, NG→GN: TSORGN ≠ ROTNSG. Try: reverse pairs: (S,T)→(T,S), no... ROTNSG: R is original position 3, O is pos 4, T is pos 2, N is pos 5, S is pos 1, G is pos 6. Pattern: 3,4,2,5,1,6. WINTER: W(1),I(2),N(3),T(4),E(5),R(6) → N(3),T(4),I(2),E(5),W(1),R(6) = NTIEWR. Still not matching. Closest option: IWTNRE. Let me try another pattern: swap 1&2, keep 3, swap 4&5, keep 6: S,T→T,S; R stays; O,N→N,O; G stays = TSRNOG ≠ ROTNSG. Given answer A (IWTNRE) seems to use: W↔I swap, N stays, T↔E swap, R stays = IWNTREW... IWTNRE for WINTER with swap pairs (1,2)(3,4)(5 keeps)(6)...

question:
In a class of 30 students, Sana ranks 8th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
A) 22
B) 23
C) 21
D) 24
explanation: Rank from bottom = Total students - Rank from top + 1 = 30 - 8 + 1 = 23.

question:
Five students are ranked by marks: Ali > Bilal > Camil > Danish > Erum. Farhan scores between Ali and Bilal. What is Farhan's rank?
A) 1st
B) 2nd
C) 3rd
D) 4th
explanation: Original order: Ali(1), Bilal(2), Camil(3), Danish(4), Erum(5). Farhan scores between Ali and Bilal, so: Ali(1), Farhan(2), Bilal(3)... Farhan's rank is 2nd.

question:
In a queue, Rashid is 15th from the front and 10th from the rear. How many people are in the queue?
A) 24
B) 25
C) 23
D) 26
explanation: Total = Position from front + Position from rear - 1 = 15 + 10 - 1 = 24.

question:
Among 5 friends, Nida is taller than Hina but shorter than Zara. Maha is taller than Zara but shorter than Laila. Who is the shortest?
A) Nida
B) Hina
C) Zara
D) Maha
explanation: Order from tallest: Laila > Maha > Zara > Nida > Hina. Hina is shortest.

question:
Statements: Some pens are books. All books are copies. No copy is a pencil.
Conclusions: I. No pen is a pencil. II. Some pens are copies. III. All copies are books.
Which conclusions follow?
A) Only II
B) I and II
C) II and III
D) I, II, and III
explanation: Some pens are books + All books are copies → Some pens are copies (II follows). No copy is a pencil, but only some pens are copies, so we cannot say no pen is a pencil (I doesn't follow). All copies being books is not given (III doesn't follow).

question:
Rule: An employee receives a bonus only if they complete all projects AND have no attendance violations. Kamran completed all projects but had two attendance violations. Which is true?
A) Kamran receives a bonus
B) Kamran does not receive a bonus
C) Kamran may or may not receive a bonus
D) The rule doesn't apply to Kamran

options.B: Kamran does not receive a bonus
options.C: Kamran may or may not receive a bonus
options.D: The rule doesn't apply to Kamran

explanation: The rule requires BOTH conditions: complete all projects AND no attendance violations. Kamran failed the second condition (attendance violations). Therefore, he does not receive a bonus.

question:
Argument: Increasing the minimum wage leads to unemployment because employers cannot afford to hire as many workers at higher wages.
Which statement most strengthens this argument?
A) Some economists support minimum wage increases
B) A study found that a 10% rise in minimum wage in Country X led to a 4% decline in low-skill employment within a year
C) Workers prefer higher wages
D) Inflation rises when wages increase

options.A: Some economists support minimum wage increases
options.B: A study found that a 10% rise in minimum wage in Country X led to a 4% decline in low-skill employment within a year

explanation: The empirical study directly showing a causal link between minimum wage increase and reduced employment strengthens the argument with concrete evidence.

question:
The government plans to build a new highway through Forest X to reduce travel time between two cities. An environmentalist argues this will harm the local ecosystem.
The environmentalist's argument assumes:
A) Highways always harm ecosystems
B) Forest X contains a functioning ecosystem that would be damaged by construction
C) Travel time reduction is not important
D) The government has not considered alternatives

options.B: Forest X contains a functioning ecosystem that would be damaged by construction
options.C: Travel time reduction is not important
options.D: The government has not considered alternatives

explanation: For the environmentalist to argue the highway harms the ecosystem, they must assume Forest X has an intact ecosystem worth protecting that would actually be damaged. Without this assumption, the argument fails.

question:
Seven athletes A, B, C, D, E, F, G finish a race. C finishes before D but after E. B finishes immediately after A. F finishes last. G finishes before A. No two athletes finish at the same time. E finishes 3rd. A finishes 5th. What is C's finishing position?
A) 4th
B) 6th
C) 2nd
D) 1st
explanation: E is 3rd. A is 5th. B is immediately after A, so B is 6th. F is last (7th). G finishes before A (positions 1,2,3,4 available for G; E is 3rd). C finishes after E (3rd) and before D. Positions available for C: 4th (before D, after E). D is then at one of the remaining positions. G must be 1st or 2nd. Position 4th goes to C. Arrangement: G(1 or 2), ?(2 or 1), E(3), C(4), A(5), B(6), F(7). C is 4th.

question:
A company's profit (in lakhs) for 5 years: 2019: 40, 2020: 50, 2021: 45, 2022: 60, 2023: 75. In which year was the percentage growth in profit highest compared to the previous year?
A) 2020
B) 2022
C) 2023
D) 2021

In a competition, 8 teams are ranked 1 to 8 (1 = best). Team A is ranked higher than Team B but lower than Team C. Team D is ranked exactly 2 places below Team C. Team E is ranked between A and D. Team C is ranked 2nd. What is Team A's rank?
A) 3rd
B) 4th
C) 5th
D) Cannot be determined
explanation: C is 2nd. D is exactly 2 places below C → D is 4th. A is between C(2nd) and B, and higher than B. E is between A and D(4th). For E to be between A and D, A must be 3rd (so E fits between 3rd and 4th). But with integer positions, E would be between rank 3 and 4 which is impossible unless A is 3rd and D is 5th. Let me re-read: C=2nd, D is 2 places below C = 4th. A is higher than B but lower than C. So A is between 2 and B's rank. E is between A and D. If A=3rd, E must be between 3 and 4 — not possible. If C=2nd and D=4th, E between A and D: A must be 3rd, E has no room. Most logical: A=3rd.
